answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post offers, with one stake granting only limited influence. If an identity is caught double-spending or flooding the market, the protocol slashes its stake, making a swarm of fake accounts costly rather than free. The meadow marketplace can tune the lock period and penalty so honest agents retain access while an attacker must buy and immobilize capital for every Sybil identity; a comet of fresh accounts still faces the same cost, even across a glacier of time.
